app.name: Masamong
attention.backup_stale: The last backup is {days} days old.
attention.budget_near: {pct}% of this month's budget is used.
attention.budget_reached: This month's budget (${budget}) is used up. The bot stays quiet.
attention.crash_gave_up: The service kept stopping unexpectedly ({reason}), so automatic restarts were stopped. It is running again now; check the logs.
attention.crash_restarted: The service stopped unexpectedly ({reason}) and was started again.
attention.crash_restarted_no_reason: The service stopped unexpectedly and was started again.
attention.crashed: The service stopped unexpectedly {n} times in 7 days.
attention.delivery_permission: The bot could not post a reply in <#{channel_id}>: Discord said it lacks permission. Check that it can View Channel, Send Messages and Read Message History there.
attention.discord_reconciliation: {n} saved Discord edit/delete files are waiting for recovery. Edits from Discord stay paused until they are handled. See docs/memory-operations.md §17.
attention.embed_model_changed: The embedding model changed, so memory search is empty until the blocks are prepared again.
attention.key_credit_low: Only ${left} is left on the {provider} key, less than this month's remaining budget (${room}). If the key runs out first, the bot cannot answer.
attention.key_credit_out: The {provider} key is almost out (${left} of ${limit} left). Every reply will fail soon.
attention.llm_unconfigured: No model key: the bot cannot answer.
attention.memory_scope: Memories from other rooms ({n}) were caught just before reaching an answer. The isolation between rooms has a defect; check the logs.
attention.price_unknown: Some models have no known price, so the monthly budget cannot stop their cost: {roles}. Set a price on the Connections page.
attention.restart_pending: A change waits for a restart.
attention.restore_failed: Restoring {name} failed. Safety backup {safety} is kept.
attention.restore_pending: A restore waits for a restart.
attention.servers_pending: {n} server(s) the bot was invited to wait for approval: {name}
banner.offline: Connection to the service was lost. Reconnecting; values on screen may be stale.
banner.restart_pending: The storage change applies after the service restarts.
block.auto_update_hint: Adds new messages to search every {min} minutes, within budget.
block.batch_draining_note: Nothing more is sent after the cancel or the refused submission. What is still at the provider is collected and saved, and nothing runs live meanwhile.
block.batch_note: The results are collected automatically when the provider finishes, even after you close the window or restart. This channel's Discord auto-update pauses meanwhile. Cancelling still charges and keeps what already finished.
block.batch_unknown: The provider never confirmed whether the batch sent {when} was accepted. This block is held to avoid paying twice. Check the batch list in the provider's console, then discard this batch.
block.budget_saved: Saved as this block's default budget
block.capture_global_off: Collection is off for the whole bot, so this room's new messages are not stored either.
block.capture_hint: Stores new messages from this channel, only in this server's database.
block.channels_desc: These channels search this block when they reply.
block.delete_body: {n} messages and {links} channel connections will be removed. Type the block name to delete.
block.delete_discord: Removes the collected messages and search pieces. With collection on, new messages build up again.
block.delete_kakao: Removes the imported messages and search pieces from this server and disconnects every channel. The original CSV is untouched, so you can import it again.
block.discard_batch_body: Open batches are asked to cancel and the record is removed. Work the provider already did may still be charged, and its results are not saved. You can prepare the block again afterwards.
block.mode_saved: Saved as this block's default way to run
block.name_desc: The name is also how the bot refers to this memory.
block.not_found_body: It was deleted or the address changed.
block.prepare_desc: Splits the chat into search pieces and builds search vectors and summaries.
block.quick.desc: For indexing a few new messages straight away. The preview splits this block's new messages into pieces and stores them (no model call, no cost), then reports the workload. Only a small job runs here: fewer than {n} pieces and fewer than that many message vectors, estimated at {sec} seconds or less. For anything bigger, use the background run above.
block.quick.partial: Only partly updated. See the notes below
block.quick.plan: {leaves} pieces to process ({embeds} new vectors · {cached} from cache · {sums} summaries) · {msgs} message vectors · estimated cost {cost} · about {time}
block.quick.run_failed: The run did not finish. Preview again to check the state, then retry.
block.quick.stopped: The work stopped part-way. {reason} Preview again to continue with what is left, or use the background run above.
block.quick.sync_failed: Syncing failed for {n} room(s) of this block, so the work is not finished. Try Preview again in a moment; if it keeps failing, check Logs & diagnostics.
block.quick.title: Update a little right now (no background job)
block.quick.too_big: This job is too big to run on this page: the page would wait for it and look hung on a small server. Use the background run above. (Running here is limited to under {n} pieces and an estimated {sec} seconds or less.)
block.quick.too_big_known: This block already has a lot waiting. Use the background run above.
block.quick.unprepared: A block that has not been prepared needs one full run first; use the background run above.
block.ready_note: Everything is searchable. Update when new messages arrive.
block.running_note: It continues after you close the window; cancelling keeps what is done.
blocks.batch.draining: Collecting the batches already sent ({n} items, sent {when})
blocks.batch.waiting: Waiting for the provider's batch ({n} items, sent {when})
blocks.batch_resumed: A batch for this block was already sent; following it
blocks.budget_hint: Automatically pauses when the budget limit is reached; resuming continues from the paused point.
blocks.capture_off: Collection is off, so new messages are not stored.
blocks.desc: One chat room forms one memory block. Import chat history, prepare search indexes, and link them to designated Discord channels.
blocks.empty_body: Import an exported KakaoTalk chat, or turn on collection in a Discord channel.
blocks.est.basis_fallback: Some model prices are unknown, so this is a rough estimate.
blocks.est.basis_prices: Estimated from the models' prices; the provider-reported cost is what gets recorded.
blocks.meta.memory_title: Estimated from the room's size (a fixed cost plus a cost per message), not measured. For now every room is loaded at once.
blocks.mode.batch_hint: Sent to the provider as one job at about half the price. It takes minutes to about a day. Parts it cannot batch, and anything that fails, run right after.
blocks.mode.label: How to run
blocks.mode.live_hint: Starts at once and usually finishes in minutes.
blocks.mode.unavailable: This provider cannot batch these, so it runs now.
blocks.next.needs_prep: Indexing is required before the bot can retrieve and use this memory.
blocks.next.partial: {n} new chunks are waiting to be indexed.
blocks.no_llm: No embedding model key, so it cannot be prepared.
blocks.set.budget_hint: Each block can set its own.
blocks.set.lab_hint: Compare results in the lab before changing it.
blocks.set.live_desc: Stores new messages from channels with collection on and adds them to search periodically.
blocks.set.prepare_desc: Applies to every block, from the next preparation on.
blocks.set.search_desc: How the bot searches connected blocks before it replies.
blocks.set.turn_budget_hint: Paid steps such as reranking stay within it.
blocks.silent: {n} Discord channels with no stored messages
blocks.silent_note: Once collection is on, new messages become that channel's block. Earlier messages are not fetched.
blocks.stop.budget: Paused because the budget limit was reached. Run again to process remaining data.
blocks.stop.cancelled: Task cancelled. Already indexed data has been safely preserved.
blocks.stop.index_incomplete: Only a portion was indexed. Please run the preparation task again.
blocks.stop.interrupted: Interrupted when the service stopped. Prepare again to continue.
blocks.stop.provider_error: The model provider returned an error. Try again shortly.
blocks.stop.store_error: Could not write to storage. Once storage is reachable, the next pass continues.
blocks.title: Memory blocks
cfg.access.blocked_users.hint: People the bot ignores in every server.
cfg.access.desc: Who may use the Discord admin command, who is blocked and which servers the bot answers in.
cfg.access.operators.hint: May use the Discord admin command in any server. Also editable under People & consent.
cfg.access.server_approval.hint: The bot stores and answers nothing in a newly invited server until you approve it under Servers & rooms.
cfg.access.servers.hint: The approve and revoke buttons under Servers & rooms change this list.
cfg.admin.web.bind.hint: Keep 127.0.0.1; for remote access use SSH, or a Tailscale name on the Display & access page.
cfg.admin.web.hosts.hint: Only names a proxy on this computer forwards (tailscale serve). The Display & access page allows the Tailscale name in one click.
cfg.alerts.desc: Operators (the operator IDs under Access) get a Discord DM when something needs them. Test it on the Maintenance page.
cfg.chat.tool_mode.hint: Also on the Tools page. Switch back to the planner if cost matters more.
cfg.chat.vision.hint: Only pictures attached when someone calls the bot are read. Also on the Tools page.
cfg.disaster_alerts.desc: What the bot announces from KMA in the channels it answers in. Easier to change under Tools → Disaster alerts → Operations.
cfg.dm.desc: Who can chat with the bot in Discord DMs, and how many chats a day. Easier to change on the People & access page.
cfg.dm.per_day.hint: 0 is the default (100), -1 is no limit, 1 to 100000 is a number you set.
cfg.dm.per_user_per_day.hint: 0 is the default (30), -1 is no limit, 1 to 10000 is a number you set.
cfg.features.desc: Off stops every tool of that feature
cfg.i18n.polite_default.hint: Rooms without a persona answer in a warm polite voice instead of the casual friend (Korean and Japanese). New instances start with it on; an instance from an earlier version keeps its casual voice.
cfg.instance.desc: Instance name, bot names and data location
cfg.limits.budget_alert_percent.hint: Warn when this share of the monthly budget is spent.
cfg.limits.max_concurrent_turns.hint: Replies worked on at once; more wait briefly or are turned away as busy.
cfg.memory.backfill_days.hint: How many days back to catch up on messages missed while offline, on reconnect. 0 = default 7, -1 = off, at most 30.
cfg.memory.backfill_max_messages.hint: The most messages one catch-up reads per room. 0 = default 4000.
cfg.memory.cards.hint: Facts that came up on several days are kept as a short card per person and server, and replies look at them. Off by default.
cfg.memory.day_boundary.hint: The time (HH:MM) a day starts when conversations are split by date. The default 05:00 keeps late-night talk with the previous day.
cfg.memory.derived_budget_usd.hint: 0 turns room memory off. At 80% the room state pauses first; at 100% extraction stops. Empty means 3.00 dollars.
cfg.memory.episodes.hint: Replies look at episodes made from past talk, such as plans and decisions, that bear on the current conversation. On by default.
cfg.memory.index_workers.hint: How many embedding and summary requests indexing sends at once. Default 8, 1–256. Lower it if the embedding service often says you hit its rate limit (429).
cfg.memory.person_aliases.hint: Names that mean the same person (for example a real name and a nickname).
cfg.memory.state: Use the room state in replies
cfg.memory.state.hint: Replies look at what the room is talking about now and its open questions. On by default.
cfg.participation.cooldown_sec.hint: Least time between two unasked remarks in a channel (at least 120).
cfg.participation.judge_per_hour.hint: Each judgement is one paid model call.
cfg.participation.min_score.hint: A ranking score from 0 to 1 (not a probability).
cfg.participation.mode.hint: Each channel chooses on its room page; none goes beyond this.
cfg.participation.shadow_drafts.hint: Easier to review, but each draft is another model call.
cfg.participation.wait_sec.hint: How long a question must go unanswered before the bot considers it.
cfg.retention.desc: Days each kind of record is kept. Conversation memory is never pruned by age.
cfg.retention.image_days.hint: How long pictures from the image tool are kept. 0 = default 14, -1 = forever.
cfg.tools.desc: Per-tool switches, limits and HTTP tools (easier from the Tools page)
cfg.updates.desc: Once a day the service asks GitHub whether a newer version is out. It sends only its name and version and installs nothing.
cfg.web_search.desc: The order the web search tool tries its services in. Easier to change with the arrows under Tools → Web search.
cfg.web_search.order.hint: Provider names, comma-separated (e.g. tavily, serper, kakao). Empty: every service with a key, Tavily → Linkup → Exa → Serper → Brave → TinyFish → Kakao.
checklist.title: Getting started
config.conflict_body: The latest config is loaded. Apply your change again.
conn.add_custom_invalid: Enter a name and an https API address.
conn.add_desc: Add one, then enter its key; the connection is checked right away. Keys stay in this computer's keychain or data folder.
conn.bot_none: Save the token and the bot ID is filled in for you.
conn.byok_claude: Claude only on my Anthropic key (BYOK)
conn.byok_claude_hint: Add your Anthropic key under OpenRouter settings → BYOK and set it to never use shared capacity. When that key fails, the fallback model answers instead of OpenRouter credits. Spending counts what Anthropic bills too.
conn.clear_body.image: The image tool answers "not configured". You can pick a model again.
conn.clear_body.vision: Pictures go the usual way: the response model sees them if it takes pictures, otherwise the planner and response models describe them. You can pick a model again.
conn.content_intent_hint: Needed for ! commands and 'every message' mode. Also enable it in the developer portal.
conn.custom_api_hint.anthropic: Anthropic's Messages API format (/v1/messages), Anthropic's own or another company's compatible endpoint. The key goes in both the x-api-key and the Bearer header.
conn.desc: The outside services the bot uses: model providers and models per role, keys for search and data services, and Discord.
conn.effort_hint: How long a reasoning model thinks before it answers. Lower is faster and cheaper. On the default, short checks such as name calls and follow-ups run without thinking; once you pick a level they think too, at most at Low. A level the model does not take is sent as the nearest one below.
conn.effort_hint_summary: How much the summary model thinks. On the default, summaries run without thinking, so the short output limit is not spent on it. Pick a level and they think at it, with extra output room for the thinking.
conn.embed_change_note: Changing the embedding model means indexing all memory again with the new model (it costs). Memory search pauses until then; Memory blocks shows the estimate first.
conn.embed_switch_body: A new embedding model leaves memory search empty until {leaves} pieces in {rooms} rooms are indexed again. After changing it, re-index from the Memory blocks screen.
conn.embed_switch_tokens: Indexing it again takes up to about {tokens} tokens.
conn.env_note.windows: On Windows, a service started from the Start menu or the tray icon may not see a variable set in a terminal. Save it with setx and restart the service, or store the key here instead.
conn.fb_desc: When the main model fails, these are asked from the top. A timeout, connection error, 429, 5xx, refused key, no credit, unknown model or empty answer counts as a failure; a malformed request is not passed on. A model that keeps failing is skipped for a while (10 min for key or credit problems, 1 min for 429, otherwise 1 min after 3 failures in a row).
conn.fb_model_hint: Exactly as the provider names it (e.g. deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash)
conn.fb_need_model: Every fallback needs a provider and a model name
conn.fb_none: No fallbacks. For now, when the main model fails the planner and answer models stand in for each other.
conn.fb_price_note: Leave prices empty to use the provider's list or a published price. For hosts that report none (such as OpenGateway), enter them or the calls count as free.
conn.group.data_hint: used by the weather, alert, stock and exchange-rate tools
conn.group.web_hint: used by the web search and read-a-link tools
conn.gw.check_hint: The connection looks up, but Discord has not acknowledged the heartbeat for a while. If it stays like this for a few minutes, restart the bot.
conn.gw.event_hint: A quiet server can go long without events. For reference only.
conn.gw.title: Connection check
conn.gw.unknown_hint: There is not enough information yet. Check again once the connection settles.
conn.host_note.anthropic: Anthropic's Claude models (Messages API): chat, image input and thinking effort; no embeddings, reranking or image generation. Prompt caching is not used yet.
conn.host_note.cometapi: Many vendors' models with one key; costs use reference prices.
conn.host_note.compatible: DeepSeek, a local server, or any OpenAI-style address
conn.host_note.gemini: Google's models: chat, embeddings and images; no reranking.
conn.host_note.nanogpt: Many vendors' models with one key; prices are listed.
conn.host_note.openai: OpenAI's models: chat, embeddings and images; no reranking.
conn.host_note.opengateway: Many vendors' models with one key; it shows no prices, so enter them yourself.
conn.host_note.openrouter: Many vendors' models with one key; costs come with each answer.
conn.intent_blocked: Settings use message content but the Developer Portal has it off, so Discord refuses the connection. Turn it on there or switch it off below.
conn.intent_off: Message Content is off in the Developer Portal: the bot answers mentions and commands only and remembers no conversation.
conn.intent_on: Message Content is on in the Developer Portal.
conn.invite_failed: Unable to build the invite link
conn.key_desc: The key is stored as a file in the data folder and never shown again.
conn.key_desc.windows: The key is saved as a plain file in the Masamong data folder (inside your Windows user profile) and is never shown again.
conn.key_desc_keychain: The key is stored encrypted in this Mac's keychain; config, logs and backups only hold where it is.
conn.key_hint: Applies as soon as you save.
conn.key_rejected: This key was rejected {when}. Replace it.
conn.key_unverified: {id}: the model list opens, but the key is not proven yet
conn.key_unverified_body: This service shows its models without a key. Point a role at one of its chat models and the test proves the key with a one-token request.
conn.keyless_note: Works without a key (a key unlocks the paid plan)
conn.missing_keys: {id} has no key, so {roles} do not work.
conn.model_provider_hint: Each role can use a model from any provider. Changing the provider loads that provider's models.
conn.no_list_note: This address gives no model list. Type the model name exactly as the provider's docs give it.
conn.no_list_test: {id}: reachable, but it has no model list
conn.no_list_test_body: Type the model name yourself. Point a role at one of its models and test again to prove the key with a one-token request.
conn.no_models: No models. Add the provider key first.
conn.no_tools_note: Models marked as having no tools may not suit answers and planning that use tools such as weather or search.
conn.ov.discord_no_token: On, but there is no bot token
conn.pick_model_desc: Browsing is free. Prices are per million tokens.
conn.practice_note: The practice mode's offline model. No key, no cost.
conn.price_cached: USD per million cached input tokens (optional)
conn.price_cached_hint: Input the host served from its prompt cache. Empty uses the model list API's price, then the published price, then the normal input price.
conn.price_desc: Used to count cost on hosts that do not report it, and to estimate preparation cost. Leave empty to use the provider's list.
conn.price_note: Hosts that report the actual cost (like OpenRouter) always use that.
conn.price_src.reference: Reference price (the same model on OpenRouter; the real bill may differ)
conn.price_src.unknown: Set it if the host does not report costs
conn.price_stale: This price was read over four months ago. Check the provider's pricing and set it yourself if it changed.
conn.reason_no_hint: The model list says this model does not think, so no level is sent.
conn.reason_unknown_hint: The model list does not say whether it thinks. A level it refuses is adjusted after the first refusal.
conn.reason_yes_hint: The model list says this model thinks; levels it does not take are greyed out.
conn.rec_budget_desc: Ranked by (3×input + output)÷4 from the provider's list prices, in USD per million tokens. Models with no known price and free variants are left out; known families come first.
conn.rec_budget_embed_locked: Memory is indexed, so the embedding model is not changed here. A new one needs every room indexed again: change it in the role table, then re-index from the Memory blocks screen.
conn.rec_budget_none: This provider's list has no prices, so there is no price ranking.
conn.rec_desc: From this provider's list: the newest released model for each role. Untick the roles to keep. The settings history can undo it.
conn.rec_embed_off: {leaves} memory pieces are indexed with the current embedding model, so it stays. Tick it to change it.
conn.rec_embed_on: A new embedding model leaves memory search empty until {leaves} pieces in {rooms} rooms are embedded again: up to about {tokens} tokens, about {usd}.
conn.rec_no_rerank: Reranking stays as it is: this provider has none.
conn.rec_none: Nothing in this provider's list fits a role.
conn.rec_reindex: The embedding model changed: memory needs indexing again.
conn.rec_replaced: Just changed to another model (the pick above is not applied)
conn.rec_width_why.default: The default width: it keeps search quality while using little memory and disk.
conn.rec_width_why.no_rerank: After this change no rerank model would be usable, so the full width is suggested: it finds conversation-flow questions better.
conn.rec_width_why.small_host: This device has little memory, so 1024 is suggested even without a rerank model.
conn.rejected_keys: The {id} key was rejected, so {roles} do not work.
conn.remote_desc: Manage Masamong running on a server from this computer's browser.
conn.remote_easy_hint: Run on your computer: it opens the SSH tunnel, signs in and opens the browser.
conn.remote_manual_hint: Then open http://127.0.0.1:{port} in your browser.
conn.remote_safety: The console never listens publicly; access goes through encrypted SSH, or a Tailscale name you allowed (inside your tailnet only).
conn.remove_body: Removes the provider and its key reference from settings. You can add it again.
conn.remove_in_use: The {roles} model uses this provider; switch it to another first.
conn.rerank_no_key: This provider has no key, so memory search ranks without reranking.
conn.rerank_unsupported: This provider cannot rerank, so memory search ranks without it. Pick OpenRouter to rerank.
conn.role_no_key: This provider has no key, so this role does not work.
conn.slash_hint: The command list re-syncs when tool settings change.
conn.stored_in.file: Stored in a private file (mode 0600) on the computer running Masamong
conn.stored_in.file.windows: Stored in a key file in the Masamong data folder (inside your Windows user profile)
conn.timeout_hint: If the model has not answered by then, the other chat model answers instead. Empty means 30 s for intent and 90 s for answers; raise it for a model that thinks first.
conn.timeout_invalid: Enter 5 to 600 seconds, or leave it empty.
conn.title: Connections
conn.vision_unknown_note: This provider's list does not say which models take pictures, so every model is shown. Some may not read pictures.
conn.waiting: Services you can use with a key (optional)
conn.waiting_more: More services you can use with a key (optional)
conn.width_custom_note: It is not known whether this model supports cutting its vectors to the leading part, so the width cannot be changed here. The width written in the settings file is used as it is.
conn.width_cut_done: Kept only the leading part of the stored vectors; nothing was embedded again.
conn.width_desc: Choose how much of each vector is kept. Narrower uses less memory and disk; search speed and embedding cost stay about the same.
conn.width_lower_body: Only the leading part of the stored vectors is kept, with no API call. It costs nothing and uses less memory and disk. Widening it again later means embedding everything again.
conn.width_narrow: Width: {n} (the leading part of the full {full})
conn.width_norerank: Without a rerank model, the full width finds conversation-flow questions better. On a device with little memory, keep 1024.
conn.width_opt_full: The most precise. Uses the most memory and disk.
conn.width_opt_middle: A middle width: less memory and disk than the full width.
conn.width_opt_recommended: Uses the least memory and disk while keeping search quality. With a rerank model the difference is barely noticeable.
conn.width_over: Width: {n} (a manual setting above the full width {full})
conn.width_over_note: The width written in the settings file is larger than this model's full width {full}. Going back to the full width means embedding the stored memory again; a narrower width only keeps the leading part, which costs nothing.
conn.width_raise_body: Widening it leaves memory search empty until {leaves} pieces in {rooms} rooms are embedded again at the new width. After changing it, re-index from the Memory blocks screen.
conn.width_raise_note: Widening means embedding the stored memory again (it costs). If rooms are indexed, the estimate is shown before anything changes.
conn.width_read_failed: Could not read the embedding width
conn.width_read_failed_body: The current embedding model and width could not be read, so nothing can be applied. Read them again, then choose.
conn.width_reindex: The embedding width changed: memory needs indexing again.
conn.width_stale_body: The embedding model or width was changed elsewhere. Check the current value and choose again.
conn.width_stale_title: The setting changed meanwhile, so the width change was cancelled
conn.width_unchanged: No change: the embedding width is already {n}. Nothing was cut or embedded again.
conn.width_unsupported: It is not known whether this model supports cutting its vectors to the leading part, so it uses its full width.
connect.desc: Pick the channels that search this block. It is never copied, and disconnecting deletes nothing.
connect.lead: Choose what each channel remembers. A channel always remembers its own conversation and also searches the blocks connected here.
connect.memory_off_hint: Memory is off here, so the channel will not search it.
connect.no_channels: No channels yet. Connect Discord or add a channel under Servers & rooms.
connect.own_note: The block's own channel is not listed; a channel always remembers its own conversation.
connect.own_title: A channel's own conversation is always included
connect.title: Channels for '{name}'
conv.attribution.hint: In a room where several people talk at once, the reply uses only the caller's conversation. Structure only uses rules with no model call; Off shows every recent line.
conv.banter.hint: When someone talks about the bot in fun ("the bot is broken again lol"), it answers back with one light line or an emoji. A real complaint gets no answer; at most 2 lines and 4 emoji an hour, and after a 👎 no lines for 2 hours. Record only does nothing and keeps the moments it would have answered.
conv.d.thread.closed_idle_recap: Closed: quiet for a while (recap posted)
conv.desc: How the bot tells it is being called and carries on a conversation in this room. Changes save as you make them.
conv.follow.hint: Sets whether the bot answers when the person it just answered carries on without tagging it. It is off by default, but the moments it would have answered are recorded even while off, to tune the defaults later.
conv.follow.label: Follow-up mode
conv.follow.reply_only: Only replies to the bot's message
conv.follow_max_untagged.hint: After this many untagged answers in a row the next one needs a tag and a thread is offered. Empty means 12.
conv.follow_window_sec.hint: After a reply, untagged lines inside this time count as carrying on. Empty means 90 seconds; the most is 600.
conv.log_hint: No message text is stored: only the kind of decision, its score and what people did next. It is recorded even while a feature is off, to tune the defaults.
conv.name_call: When only its name is said
conv.name_call.addressed: Only when said to the bot (default)
conv.name_call.hint: Sets how a message that only says the bot's name (no mention, no reply) is read. By default a small model tells "talking to the bot" from "talking about the bot", and the bot stays quiet when unsure.
conv.reply_shape.hint: Bubbles send two or three short paragraphs as separate messages a moment apart, like a person typing. A far longer reply shows its first part with a "more" button.
conv.thread.auto_task: Open by itself for a task (experimental)
conv.thread.hint: Under a long one-on-one exchange the bot shows a button to move it into a thread. "Open by itself for a task" lets the bot open one itself for a multi-step task (experimental).
conv.thread.label: Opening threads
conv.thread_follow: Who it answers in a thread
conv.thread_follow.hint: Sets who the bot answers without a tag inside a thread it opened. By default the people it was talking with; lines aimed at someone else are left alone.

people.note: Names come from the fortune profile or the latest stored message. Only the person can agree, in Discord; here you can withdraw and delete.
people.policies.desc: Each feature asks separately. A new policy version needs a new agreement.
people.policies.title: Consent policies
people.prefs.title: Personal settings
people.servers.desc: People seen in stored Discord messages. Message text is not shown.
people.servers.empty_body: There are no stored messages for this server, or no people match the search.
people.servers.readonly: This Discord person has no consent or settings record. Stored conversation text is not shown here.
people.servers.title: People by server
people.servers.top_limit: Showing up to {n} recently seen people per server.
people.servers.users_row_hint: This person has consent, subscription or settings records. Opens them.
people.tab.users_desc: People with consent, subscription or settings records. Open a row to withdraw or delete.
perm.create_public_threads_why: Needed for the offer to move a chat into a thread.
persona.apply_desc: The chosen rooms use this persona from the next reply. Every room can have its own.
persona.bundles_desc: Missing strings fall back to English.
persona.default_chip_hint: New rooms of this language use this persona by default.
persona.delete_body: Deletes {id}. Only possible when no room uses it.
persona.delete_in_use: Rooms use it. Switch them to another persona first.
persona.desc: Make personas and give each room its own. Change them from Servers & rooms, or with Apply to rooms on a card.
persona.err.id: IDs are 2–41 characters, starting with a lowercase letter.
persona.err.label: Enter a name.
persona.hide_hint: Built-in personas are hidden instead of deleted; restore them any time. Hiding a voice also takes its newer version (_v2) out of the defaults for new rooms.
persona.hide_in_use: Rooms use it. Switch them to another persona first.
persona.id_hint: Made from the name. The value config files use for this persona.
persona.label: Name
persona.lang_hint: Only personas for the console/system language are shown. Switch the language here to manage personas in another language.
persona.langs_desc: Languages of the conversations. They set search rules (particles, stop words). Mix several with commas.
persona.locale_hint: The language replies use in rooms with this persona.
persona.names_desc: Names people call the bot. The first appears in prompts; any of them counts as a mention.
persona.none_lang: No personas for this language yet. Add one with New persona.
persona.scope_note: A persona never widens tool access or memory scope.
persona.style_hint: The persona part of the reply prompt. {bot} becomes the bot's name.
persona.title: Persona & language
persona.tpl.brief: You are {bot}, a Discord bot. Answer with only the point, in one or two sentences, without greetings or filler.
persona.tpl.cheer: You are {bot}, a Discord bot. Speak warmly, notice how people feel and encourage them, without overdoing the praise.
persona.tpl.friend: You are {bot}, a Discord bot. Talk casually and briefly, like a friend who has been around this room for a long time. Keep jokes light and say so when you do not know.
persona.tpl.polite: You are {bot}, a Discord bot. Always answer politely and accurately. Use a short list only when it helps.
persona.try_desc: Gets a reply with these instructions, using the chosen room's memory and rules. Nothing goes to Discord. Model calls are billed.
persona.try_no_rooms: No room to try in. Add one under Servers & rooms first.
pm.desc: What the bot keeps about this person in one server. Each server keeps its own.
pm.empty: Nothing is kept about this person in this server.
pm.forget_body: Deletes the items and card kept about this person in this server and takes them out of shared conversations. The original messages stay. This cannot be undone.
pm.forget_preview: {items} items · removed from {episodes} conversations · {cards} card items
pm.forget_title: Forget what is kept about this person?
pm.no_servers: The bot is not in any server yet.
pm.stale: It changed in the meantime, so nothing was deleted. Check again
pm.title: Memory in a server
practice.badge_title: Practice mode: a separate instance with sample data
practice.banner_body: Nothing here touches the real bot, Discord or costs. The model is an offline practice one.
practice.home_body: A sample chat between four invented friends is loaded. Ask questions and change rooms, tools and sources freely.
practice.maint_note: Practice mode disables what changes the real installation: restart, stop, restore and autostart.
practice.reset_body: Clears practice changes and reloads the sample conversation.
practice.sample_q: Who said they'd bring the tent for camping?
rem.repeat.monthly_last: Day {day} of every month at {time} (the last day in shorter months)
rem.room_desc: Reminders people asked for here. Only the person who asked can set or change one, in Discord.
rem.room_empty: No reminders asked for here. In Discord, try “/remind when: tomorrow 3pm what: meeting”.
rem.title: Reminders
rm.budget.off_hint: The budget is 0, so no room memory is made.
rm.budget.ok_hint: At 80% of the budget room state updates pause first; at 100% episode extraction stops. It counts from zero each month.
rm.budget.paused_hint: The budget reached 80%, so room state updates are paused. Episodes continue up to 100%.
rm.budget.stopped_hint: The budget is used up, so no new episodes are made either. Raise the budget or wait for next month.
rm.budget_desc: What building room states and episodes cost. Counted apart from reply costs.
rm.empty_body: They are made in the background once a conversation wraps up. For a KakaoTalk chat, start it from the Memory blocks page.
rm.episodes_desc: Plans, decisions and events picked from conversations. Each sentence points to the messages it came from.
rm.evidence_hint: Source messages are read from storage each time you open this. Deleted messages are not shown.
rm.ex.blocked_off: The room memory budget is 0, so nothing can be made.
rm.ex.blocked_stopped: This month's budget is used up.
rm.ex.cap_hint: Stops before spending more than this. It is separate from the monthly budget, and whichever is reached first stops the run.
rm.ex.desc: First the size and cost are estimated. The estimate is free and saves nothing.
rm.ex.empty: There is no conversation of two or more messages, so there is nothing to extract.
rm.ex.hint: Pick plans, decisions and events out of this chat.
rm.ex.note: Starting queues it and it continues in the background, even if you close this window.
rm.ex.over: The estimate is more than what is left. It will stop when the budget is reached, and the rest can be continued later.
rm.ex.remaining: Room memory budget left this month
rm.ex.title: Extract room memory for {name}
rm.ex.toast.queued: Queued. It continues in the background
rm.forget_body: Once forgotten, this episode and its items cannot be restored.
rm.forget_hidden: ({n} of them are already hidden because their source is gone)
rm.forget_keeps: The original messages are not deleted, and this conversation will not be turned into the episode again.
rm.no_rooms_body: Set up a channel under Servers & rooms or import a KakaoTalk chat and it shows up here.
rm.regen_hint: Many of its source messages were deleted or changed, so this episode will be rebuilt from what is left.
rm.set.desc: The budget and day boundary of the background work that builds room states and episodes.
rm.set.title: Room memory
rm.state_desc: A compressed note of what is going on in this room right now.
rm.state_empty_body: It is made once the room has been quiet for a while and enough new messages have piled up. It is not made when the budget is 0 or past 80%.
rm.state_kakao: Room state exists for Discord channels only. Imported KakaoTalk chats get episodes only.
rm.state_ref: A compressed summary for reference. It is not the original text and can be wrong.
role.image_hint: Draws pictures for the image tool. Leave it empty to keep image generation off
role.planner_hint: Decides which tools and memory to use
role.vision_hint: This model reads and describes pictures members send, even when the response model takes pictures itself; if it fails, pictures go the usual way. Leave it empty to keep the usual way
room.attachments_desc: Stores files for this room only. Import and index them from Sources, then add the resulting memory source.
room.attachments_note: Staging alone does not make it searchable. Finish import and indexing.
room.backfill_desc: Reads messages sent while the bot was offline back from Discord into memory. On reconnect it catches up automatically, up to {days} days.
room.backfill_needs_capture: Turn on storing live messages and save first.
room.backfill_skip.never_captured: Skipped: nothing stored since capture was turned on.
room.backfill_skip.no_history: Skipped: history could not be read from Discord (check the connection or permissions).
room.backfill_truncated: Stopped at the per-run maximum. Run again to continue.
room.blocks_desc: Besides its own conversation, this room searches the blocks connected here. Nothing is merged.
room.capture_hint: New messages here go into the memory index. The global capture switch must also be on.
room.collect_desc: How much of what the bot did here is logged. Message text is never logged.
room.copy_desc: Overwrites only the chosen parts with this room's saved settings. Connected memory sources and staged files are not copied.
room.copy_unsaved: Unsaved changes are not copied. Save first.
room.disaster_alerts_hint: New earthquakes and weather warnings are posted here. What is announced is set under Tools → Disaster alerts → Operations.
room.disaster_alerts_off_respond: A room the bot does not answer in gets no alerts either.
room.invite_desc: A server admin adds the bot, or grants its permissions again, with this link. It asks only for what the bot uses, never Administrator.
room.logging_hint: Sets how much of this room's messages and answers the conversation log keeps. It applies to conversations from now on; ones already stored stay as they are. No text stored keeps timing, tools, cost and outcome only; Text of errors only keeps the words of turns that failed. The model, tool and delivery call records hold no text and are always kept. Log files never contain message text or user IDs either way.
room.memory_desc: Whether replies here look up past conversations, and whether this room's new messages are stored.
room.memory_use_hint: Off: replies here never search past conversations.
room.not_found_body: The room is not on Discord or not set up yet.
room.pause_desc: Stops replies and commands here only.
room.perms_desc: What the bot needs to read and reply here. You get an alert when one disappears.
room.perms_fix: Grant the missing ones in Discord: Server Settings → Roles, or the channel's permissions.
room.persona_edit: Edit under Persona & language (applies to every room)
room.persona_hint: A persona never widens tool access or memory scope.
room.respond_desc: When and how the bot answers here.
room.rules_hint: {n}/2000 characters. Added to the reply prompt as written.
room.summary_desc: Summarizes the recent stored conversation; later updates fold in only new messages. The same summary as the Discord command.
room.summary_needs_capture: Turn on storing live messages to have something to summarize.
room.thread_missing: Thread offers are on for this room, but the bot lacks the permissions below, so the offer button will not appear until they are granted: {perms}
room.timeline_desc: What happened when, across this room's memory (its own conversation and connected sources).
room.tools_desc: Default follows the global tool setting. On or off applies to this room only.
room.try_desc: Get a reply with the persona and rules as edited, using this room's memory. Nothing is sent to Discord or mixed into the conversation log. Model calls are billed.
room.try_empty: Replies show up here. Save with the bar below when you like them.
room.try_ph: Say something as someone in this room. Enter to send
rooms.add_desc: You can set up a room by ID before Discord connects.
rooms.block_attached: Source added to this room's memory
rooms.block_detached: Source removed from this room's memory
rooms.block_failed: Unable to change the memory view
rooms.bulk_pending_note: {n} of the selected rooms are in a server that is not approved yet. They only answer once it is.
rooms.channel.unnamed: Discord has not reported this channel's name
rooms.desc: For each room: when the bot answers and which persona, memory and tools it uses.
rooms.empty_body: Channels appear once Discord connects. Before that, add rooms by ID.
rooms.log.auto: Automatic (a channel named logs, if any)
rooms.log.channel_hint: Keep the log channel visible to the server's managers only.
rooms.log.deleted_text.hint: The deleted message's text and attached file names are posted too. Only messages Masamong saw recently or stored have their text. It is still removed from Masamong's memory; the text stays only as a post in this log channel.
rooms.log.deletes.hint: The author, channel and time are posted. A bot's messages and the log channel's own are left out; many deleted at once become one entry.
rooms.log.desc: Masamong posts what happened in this server to a log channel: a deleted message (who wrote it, where, when and what it said) and problems such as a reply or a reminder that failed or a missing permission. It starts off; Automatic uses a channel named logs, as the previous Masamong did.
rooms.log.problems.hint: A reply that failed, a tool such as search that failed in a reply (partial error), a reminder, scheduled task or disaster alert that could not be posted, and a missing channel permission. The same problem is posted once per 15 minutes.
rooms.log.state_off_logs: Off: this server has a logs channel, so Automatic posts there
rooms.log.test_failed: Could not post the test entry
rooms.log.test_ok: Test entry posted to the log channel
rooms.log.title: Server log
rooms.privacy.card_channel_only: Use notes only where they came from
rooms.privacy.card_channel_only.hint: A person note is used only in the channel (and its threads) it came from, not in other channels of the same server.
rooms.privacy.desc: These are off by default because the bot is meant for friends' servers, where remembering freely is the point. Turn on only what a more careful server needs. Servers never share people, and deletion and withdrawal always reach derived memory, whatever you pick here.
rooms.privacy.no_hearsay: Skip notes made from what others said
rooms.privacy.no_hearsay.hint: What one person said about another is left out of the room memory; only what people said about themselves is used.
rooms.privacy.no_sensitive: Keep sensitive things out of notes
rooms.privacy.no_sensitive.hint: Health, romance, money, religion, politics and the like are not kept by "remember this" or as person notes. Sorting them uses a little of the derived-memory budget.
rooms.privacy.own_card_only: Person notes only for the person talking
rooms.privacy.own_card_only.hint: A reply uses only the note of the person who called the bot, not those of others in the conversation.
rooms.privacy.title: Strict privacy (optional)
rooms.respond_hint.always: Considers every message. Costs the most.
rooms.respond_hint.command: Reacts to ! and slash commands only; no conversation.
rooms.respond_hint.mention: Answers when mentioned or called by name.
rooms.search: Find by channel name or ID
rooms.select_hint: Tick several channels and switch them on or off together from the bar at the bottom of the screen.
rooms.server.approval_hint: When on, a server the bot is newly invited to waits here until you approve it; servers with rooms set up are approved already. When off, the bot works in every server it is invited to.
rooms.server.desc: Discord servers the bot is in. In a server that is not approved it stores nothing and answers nothing.
rooms.server.leave_body: The bot leaves this server. Its settings and memory are kept; if it is invited again you can approve it.
rooms.server.pending_body: Until approved, the bot stores no messages here and does not answer; slash commands get a waiting notice.
rooms.server.pending_note: {n} server(s) wait for approval. Approve servers you know; decline the others to take the bot out.
rooms.server.title: Servers
rooms.title: Servers & rooms
rooms.tool_saved: Tool setting saved for this room
rstyle.approved_off: This room's setting is off, so it is not used until you turn it on.
rstyle.approved_on: It is used from the next reply.
rstyle.approved_unused: The setting is off, so it is not used right now.
rstyle.budget_spent: This month's room memory budget is used up. Raise it in the room memory settings or try again next month.
rstyle.built_body: Preview it below, then approve or reject it.
rstyle.cost_note: Analyzing makes one model call, paid from this month's derived memory budget (room memory). The result is only a proposal and is not used until you approve it.
rstyle.desc: Tunes the bot's tone and length to how this room talks. An experimental feature that only uses a note you approve.
rstyle.evidence_hint: How many messages this came from. Names and the messages themselves are not shown.
rstyle.fact.approval: Nothing is used until you approve it.
rstyle.fact.delete: It stops when a source message is deleted or edited.
rstyle.fact.numbers: Numbers such as length, laughs, emoji and languages are counted without a model.
rstyle.fact.people: Slang, nicknames and jokes are only picked from messages of at least two people.
rstyle.fact.weekly: It is refreshed weekly as a proposal only, never applied by itself.
rstyle.none: Nothing analyzed yet. Analyze this room to see how it talks in numbers.
rstyle.not_enough_toast: Not enough messages, so nothing was analyzed
rstyle.on_nothing: On, but no note is approved yet, so replies are unchanged.
rstyle.setting.hint: On, the approved note is added to replies so their tone and length fit this room.
rstyle.stale: A message this note was based on was edited or deleted, so the note is no longer used. Analyze again to get a new proposal.
rstyle.stats_fresh: Just counted from {messages} messages by {people} people
rstyle.stats_saved: From the latest analysis: {messages} messages by {people} people
rstyle.title: Room style
rstyle.too_few: Only {count} messages so far. At least {min} are needed.
rstyle.try_hint: The bot answers it twice, once without the note and once with it. That is two model calls from the same budget.
rstyle.try_ph: e.g. what should we eat tonight?
savebar.label: Unsaved changes
savebar.leave: You have unsaved changes. Leave this page?
settings.apply_body: Replaces the current config. You can go back from the change history.
settings.current_yaml_desc: No secrets inside; keys are stored as references.
settings.desc: Every setting lives here. Current revision r{rev}.
settings.history_desc: Every change from the console, CLI or Discord. Secrets and messages are never recorded.
settings.import_desc: Paste another instance's config, check the difference, then apply.
settings.managed_on: This is easier to manage on the {page} page.
settings.owner: This is easier to change on the {page} page, which checks the values and explains them.
settings.readonly: Part of the installation; not changed here.
settings.rollback_body: Restores revision r{rev}. The rollback is recorded as a new revision.
settings.savebar_note: Saving creates a new revision and records it.
settings.snap_confirm_body: The current config stays in the change log and can be restored.
settings.snap_list_desc: Restoring applies as a new revision in the change log. Instance name and console address stay.
settings.snap_new_desc: Name the current config before big changes and restore it in one step.
settings.title: Settings & history
settings.tz_hint: Pick from the list or type an IANA name (e.g. Asia/Seoul).
settings.usd_invalid: Enter an amount of 0 or more (e.g. 10.00).
setup.discord.body: Paste the bot token from the Discord developer portal. The bot signs in after the service restarts.
setup.discord.invite: Invite the bot to a server
setup.discord.invite_hint: Once the token is saved the bot ID comes from Discord and you can make the link. It asks only for the permissions the bot uses. A newly invited server works after you approve it under Servers & rooms.
setup.discord.restart_hint: The bot connects after a restart.
setup.discord.title: Connect the Discord bot
setup.discord.token_hint: Developer Portal → Bot → Reset Token. Leave empty to keep the current token.
setup.model.body: Enter a key for the AI provider used for answers, planning, summaries and embeddings. It stays on this computer and is never shown again. Once it works, each role gets that provider's newest model.
setup.model.host_note.anthropic: Anthropic: Claude models directly through the Messages API. No embeddings, reranking or image generation, so fill those roles from another provider. Prompt caching is not used yet.
setup.model.host_note.cometapi: CometAPI: many vendors' models with one key (about 80% of official prices). It lists no prices, so the same model's OpenRouter price is used as a reference. No reranking.
setup.model.host_note.gemini: Google Gemini: chat, embeddings and images with one key. No reranking, so memory search ranks without it.
setup.model.host_note.nanogpt: NanoGPT: many vendors' models with one key, prices listed. Pictures go through its image endpoint. No reranking.
setup.model.host_note.openai: OpenAI: chat, embeddings and images with one key. No reranking, so memory search ranks without it.
setup.model.host_note.opengateway: OpenGateway: many vendors' models with one key (Sionic AI, Seoul). Its replies carry no price or cost, so enter prices when you use it as a fallback. No reranking.
setup.model.host_note.openrouter: Recommended: many vendors' models with one key, including reranking for memory search.
setup.model.invalid_body: The provider did not accept this key. Copy it again from its key page and paste it here.
setup.model.key_hint: Checked as soon as you save.
setup.model.title: Connect a model
setup.practice_hint: Look around with sample data before setting up.
setup.protect.fact_local: The console listens on {bind}. Other computers cannot reach it.
setup.protect.fact_ssh: Manage a remote server from this computer's browser over SSH or a Tailscale name you allowed. How is on the Display & access page.
setup.protect.fact_token: Opening Masamong from its {tray} signs in with a one-time link.
setup.protect.title: The console is already protected
setup.rail_lead: A few steps get the bot answering in one room. Stop any time and pick up where you left off.
setup.room.body: Pick a server channel and when the bot answers. Add more rooms later under Servers & rooms.
setup.room.id_hint: With Developer Mode on, right-click the server or channel and choose Copy ID.
setup.room.ids_invalid: Server and channel IDs are 5–25 digits.
setup.room.title: Pick a room for the bot
setup.test.body: The answer stays in this console; nothing is sent to Discord.
setup.test.cost_note: This test calls the model once (usually under $0.001).
setup.test.needs_key: Connect a model key to try a conversation.
setup.test.title: Say something to Masamong
setup.welcome.body: Settings and history are stored only in this computer's data folder. The outside services the bot uses (AI models, weather, search) get only what an answer needs; the Connections page lists them and turns them off.
setup.welcome.bot_lang_hint: New rooms start in this language with its built-in persona. You can change it per room or in Settings at any time.
setup.welcome.instance_hint: A name that tells bots apart. Lowercase letters work best.
setup.welcome.title: Welcome to Masamong
signin.logout_body: This browser is signed out. To come back, run one of these in a terminal on the computer running Masamong. Closing the window without signing out is fine too.
signin.open: Open it again on this computer (opens signed in)
signin.signed_out: Signed out. Use one of the ways below to come back.
signin.token: Print the access token (paste what it shows)
sources.export_locale_hint: Used to skip system lines such as deleted messages or photos.
sources.preview_hint: Check period, people and duplicates before importing (free).
sources.pv.duplicate: This file is already fully in this room; no need to import it again.
sources.server_path_hint: For a file already on a remote server, enter its path instead of uploading.
sources.timezone_hint: KakaoTalk times have no zone; they are read in this one.
stats.cost_desc: As reported by the provider, else estimated. Days are UTC.
stats.desc: How conversations, tools and cost change over time, in the instance time zone.
stats.quality_desc: Quality is not inferred from operations stats; judge and compare in the answer lab.
stats.report.desc: Summarizes conversations, cost, tools and operations for a period; download as Markdown or JSON.
stats.report.title: {instance} report
stats.stored.hint: Messages, jobs and polls stored so far, whatever the period. Counting takes a while on a large history, so it only runs when you ask.
stats.stored.title: Stored in total
stats.title: Statistics
stats.turns_desc: Stacked by outcome. Lab turns are excluded.
stopped.body: The bot no longer answers on Discord and the console is off. Start it again with the command below on this computer, or from the {tray}.
stopped.stopping_body: Finishing replies and jobs in progress. One moment.
stopped.title: The service has stopped
stopped.waiting: This page reloads by itself when the service is back.
tool.aliases_hint: Comma-separated. Empty keeps the built-in words.
tool.defaults_hint: Used when the bot or a command leaves a value out. Empty fields keep the tool's own default.
tool.defaults_invalid: Default parameters must be a JSON object.
tool.defaults_json_hint: Only for values the form does not show. Empty keeps the tool's own defaults.
tool.delete_body: The tool and its ! command are removed. Usage history stays.
tool.desc.activity.ranking: Who sent the most messages in this channel, by period. Only counts are kept, never the text; people who withdrew memory consent are not counted.
tool.desc.chat.respond: Answers in rooms. Limits cap how many replies are sent.
tool.desc.disasters.query: Weather warnings and disaster alerts in Korea (KMA, Korea only).
tool.desc.finance.fx: Exchange rates for a base currency.
tool.desc.fortune.query: Today's, this month's and this year's fortune, and zodiac readings. In a server only the summary shows; details are private.
tool.desc.fortune.subscribe: Register a birthday and get a morning fortune by DM. Needs fortune consent.
tool.desc.help.version: Tells what the bot can do.
tool.desc.images.generate: Draws a picture from a description with the image model role, one at a time.
tool.desc.memory.search: Finds people, events and nicknames in this room's past conversations.
tool.desc.notices.status: Shows the notices of your Korean university that fit your profile (Korea only).
tool.desc.notices.subscribe: Subscribe to a Korean university's notices or transfer notices and get a daily DM (Korea only). Needs notice consent.
tool.desc.places.search: Finds shops and places in Korea on Kakao Map (name, address, phone, map link; Korea only) with the Kakao web search key.
tool.desc.polls.create: Posts a poll in the room.
tool.desc.reminders.propose: Ask like "remind me tomorrow at 3pm"; the person who asked confirms the time and where it goes (DM or the channel). It can repeat (daily, weekly, monthly, every N hours), and works in conversation too.
tool.desc.reminders.update: See, reschedule, pause or resume (repeating) or cancel reminders still to come.
tool.desc.search.web: Finds news and current information on the web with the search services that have keys (Tavily, Linkup, Exa, Serper, Kakao), in your order, moving on when one fails. Not the same as Memory search, which looks through this room's past chat.
tool.desc.summaries.channel: Summarizes this room's recent conversation, folding in only new messages later.
tool.desc.transfer.recent: Recent transfer admission notices from Korean university admission boards (Korea only).
tool.desc.weather.query: Current weather and a 7-day forecast: KMA in Korea, Open-Meteo everywhere else.
tool.desc.web.read: Reads the page behind a link in the message for the answer: the article without menus or ads (Jina Reader), 20 a minute without a key. Links go to an outside service, so it stays off until you turn it on.
tool.description_hint: Empty keeps the built-in text. Up to 600 characters.
tool.http_desc: The address this tool calls and how results are trimmed.
tool.http_safety: Requests only go to this host. The model cannot redirect them, and the key never appears in results or errors.
tool.limits_desc: After the cap the tool refuses for the rest of the day, in the instance time zone.
tool.no_provider: This tool uses no external service.
tool.not_implemented_body: This tool has no working implementation yet, so it cannot be enabled or run.
tool.optin.web.read: When on, links posted in chat are sent to Jina Reader (an outside service) to fetch the page. Private network addresses and links with a username or password are never sent, but a link that opens for anyone who has it (a shared document) cannot be told apart.
tool.planner_desc: Text the planner uses to decide when to call this tool.
tool.poll_participant_hint: Use an arbitrary key for this test rather than a display name or account ID.
tool.prov_note.brave: Independent search with its own index; news search and page extracts for deep searches ($5 free credit a month, $5 per 1,000)
tool.prov_note.exa: Neural search: good at picking high-quality pages on a topic
tool.prov_note.jina_reader: Reads a page without menus or ads: 20 a minute without a key, more with one
tool.prov_note.kakao_search: Daum web search: strongest on Korean pages, snippets only
tool.prov_note.kma: Korean current weather, warnings and earthquakes (API Hub key)
tool.prov_note.linkup: Search for AI: page text from trusted sources
